python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# 1996 New Aa municipal bond yields
yields = [5.41, 5.41, 5.57, 5.72, 5.73, 5.82, 5.82, 5.69, 5.62, 5.53, 5.47, 5.47]

# Calculate month-to-month log returns
log_returns = []
for i in range(1, len(yields)):
    lr = math.log(yields[i] / yields[i-1])
    log_returns.append(lr)
    print(f"{i+1:2d}/{i:2d}: {yields[i]:.2f} / {yields[i-1]:.2f} = {yields[i]/yields[i-1]:.4f}, ln = {lr:.6f}")

print(f"\nTotal log returns: {len(log_returns)}")

# Sort returns for percentile calculation
sorted_returns = sorted(log_returns)
print("\nSorted log returns:")
for i, r in enumerate(sorted_returns):
    print(f"  Rank {i+1}: {r:.6f}")

# Nearest-rank method for 5th percentile
# Rank = ceil(p * n) where p = 0.05 and n = number of returns
n = len(log_returns)
rank = math.ceil(0.05 * n)
print(f"\nn = {n}, rank = ceil(0.05 * {n}) = ceil({0.05*n}) = {rank}")

# 5th percentile (worst return) is at position rank-1 (0-indexed)
percentile_5 = sorted_returns[rank - 1]
print(f"5th percentile (VaR) log return: {percentile_5:.6f}")

# Convert to simple percentage (expm1 gives equivalent simple return)
simple_return = math.expm1(percentile_5)
print(f"Simple return: {simple_return:.6f} = {simple_return*100:.2f}%")

# Absolute value as percentage loss
var_percentage = abs(simple_return * 100)
print(f"\n95% one-month VaR: {var_percentage:.2f}%")
EOF
